hooks.text: Our Milky Way is being hauled toward a cosmic monster.
Space expands everywhere, but our galaxy rushes toward one spot.
Over 8,000 galaxies are pulling our Milky Way toward them.

title: The Monster Pulling Our Galaxy
description: Discover the Shapley Supercluster, a colossal concentration of over 8,000 galaxies hauling our Milky Way toward it.

beats.text: Our Milky Way is being hauled toward a cosmic monster.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the Milky Way galaxy in space, NASA, 2020

beats.text: Most people think the universe expands equally in every direction.
beats.visual: Diagram showing large-scale cosmic web structure, 2018

beats.text: American astronomer Harlow Shapley found a massive cluster hiding there in 1930.
It sits roughly 650 million light-years away in Centaurus.
beats.visual: Map of galaxy distribution in the Centaurus region, 2010
queries: Atlas of the Universe Shapley Supercluster

beats.text: This colossal structure packs over 8,000 galaxies together.
beats.visual: Planck satellite composite image of the core of the Shapley Supercluster, 2013

beats.text: It holds ten million billion times the mass of the Sun.
beats.visual: X-ray emission image of the Shapley Supercluster by eROSITA, 2021

beats.text: That immense gravity keeps hauling our Milky Way toward the monster.
beats.visual: Artist concept of galaxy clusters merging in a supercluster, 2019

better_than_last: This episode applies the myth_vs_fact structure to a massive cosmic scale topic, ensuring every beat strictly ties back to the verified research claims while maintaining a seamless loop back to the hook image.
